deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): V is a finite-dimensional real vector space and (H_i)_{i∈I} a finite family of hyperplanes. For each H, D_H = {H, V'_H, V''_H} is the three-element partition of V into the hyperplane and its two open half-spaces; it is viewed as F_3 = {0, ±1}, with H as 0. The map φ: S → E = ∏ D_{H_i} sends a point of the sphere S (rays of V; the previous page writes V*, see errors) to its sign vector. Σ = φ(S) is the set of realised sign vectors, and Z*_α = φ^{-1}(α) are the open cells (relatively open convex cones) of the arrangement.

This page proves the closure formula for cells. Each closed half-space is the open half-space together with H_i. Hence the closure of Z*_α is the union of the Z*_β with β ∈ Σ and k_i(β) ≤ k_i(α) for every i. Here k_i: E → D_{H_i} are the coordinate functions, and D_{H_i} carries the order 0 < α'_i, 0 < α''_i, with α'_i and α''_i incomparable (the 'V' picture). E gets the product order and Σ the induced order. In modern terms this is the face poset of the arrangement, i.e. the covector poset of the realisable oriented matroid with the order 0 < + and 0 < −.

Grothendieck then puts on Σ the 'topologie infimum', whose closed sets are the down-sets: the Alexandrov topology in which open sets are up-sets. In it, β ≤ α iff β ∈ closure{α}, and closure(Z*_α) = Z*_{closure{α}}, with Z*_A := ∪_{α∈A} Z*_α. The next page generalises this to closure(Z*_A) = Z*_{closure A}. It concludes that Σ indexes a stratification of the sphere with connected strata satisfying the frontier axiom; equivalently, φ: S → Σ is continuous for this topology.

Purpose: to set up the combinatorial (sign-vector) description of hyperplane arrangements, as a model for the 'systèmes de pseudo-droites' that are the subject of the cote.
errors: No mathematical error on this page: the closure formula is correct for central arrangements, using that the closure of an intersection of open half-spaces and hyperplanes is the corresponding intersection of closed half-spaces and hyperplanes when that intersection is nonempty.

Notational slip inherited from the previous page: the hyperplanes H_i live in V, so the sign map should be defined on the sphere of V (the rays of V), not on S = V*/R*+. Equivalently, the H_i should be taken in V*.
Small notational inconsistencies: Z vs Z*, and the product is written ∏ D_i or D_I instead of ∏ D_{H_i}.

ideas.what: Sign vectors in {0,+,−}^I indexing the cells of a real hyperplane arrangement; the face poset with 0 < ±; closure of a cell = union of cells with smaller sign vector
ideas.modern_name: Covectors / face poset of a (realisable) oriented matroid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folkman–Lawrence 1978, Bland–Las Vergnas 1978, Edmonds–Mandel; earlier arrangement combinatorics by Zaslavsky (1975) and others

ideas.what: Alexandrov ('infimum') topology on the finite poset Σ, with closed sets = down-sets, making the sign map S → Σ continuous and expressing closures of unions of strata as closures in Σ
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified space (stratification over a poset with its Alexandrov topology), frontier condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov 1937 (finite topologies); the modern use for stratified spaces appears e.g. in Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame stratified spaces but not, as far as I know, in this poset form

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats an arrangement's stratification as a continuous map to a finite poset carrying the Alexandrov topology (closed sets = down-sets). This is exactly the later 'stratification over a poset' convention used in exit-path / higher-categorical treatments of stratified spaces. Here it is applied to oriented-matroid face posets in the context of pseudoline systems. The idea itself is standard, so this is at most a minor anticipation.
missed.quote: d'où une "top. infimum" sur Σ, dont les fermés sont les parties A de Σ telles que α∈A, β≤α ⇒ β∈A
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck, around 1981, was approaching pseudoline arrangements through poset-indexed stratifications, consistent with his tame-topology programme; mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard face-poset and closure description of hyperplane arrangements (oriented matroid covectors), rediscovered independently. It is correct but well known by 1978.
transcription_corrections: First line: the left margin is a crossed-out, unreadable note. The opening reads roughly 'On trouve que, vu la construction (?) des ½ espaces fermés …'; 'l'construction' is a misreading.
The superscript insertion 'qui contiennent Z_i' probably refers to the closed half-spaces containing Z*_α rather than 'Z_i'.
The product reads E = ∏_{i∈I} D_I in the image (meaning D_{H_i}), not D_i.
The order picture shows α'_i and α''_i above 0 (a 'V' with 0 at the bottom), with the note 'α', α'' les deux éléments ≠ 0 de D_{H_i}'.
